item.title: Colin Webber
item.description: Colin Webber is an active member of the Cape Town chess community, balancing his own journey as an “adult improver” with his passion for supporting the game. A former chess parent—his son Ethan no longer plays competitively—Colin has stayed deeply connected to the sport through both playing and service. He currently serves as the Technical Officer and Webmaster of Steinitz Chess Club, where he helps manage the club’s digital presence and supports its ongoing growth. Alongside his technical contributions, Colin enjoys encouraging and mentoring young players, drawing on his experiences as both a parent and competitor. His enthusiasm for lifelong learning and his commitment to fostering talent make him a valuable part of the Steinitz family.

item.title: Kenneth Willenberg
item.description: Kenneth Sean “Kenny” Willenberg is a South African Candidate Master (CM), currently regarded as one of the country’s strongest players. A product of Steinitz Chess Club and the proud Willenberg chess-playing legacy, Kenny has built a reputation for consistent success in both national closed championships and local league competitions. Once crowned South African Under-20 Champion, he has made multiple appearances at the SA Closed Championship, firmly establishing himself as one of the nation’s leading players early in his career. Beyond his own competitive achievements, Kenny has dedicated himself to coaching and talent development, working through programs at Curro Durbanville and Reddam House Durbanville. He was the originator of the Curro Cup, South Africa’s first online schools chess tournament, which has since grown into a landmark event on the scholastic calendar. His impact as a coach was most prominently seen at the 2025 Top Schools competition, where his Reddam U9 team not only placed first in their division but also swept all six board prizes—a rare and dominant feat. Balancing competitive strength with a passion for mentorship, Kenny continues to inspire both on and off the board, making him a highly respected figure in South African chess.
